summary: 47-year-old woman on day 9 of her third cycle of adjuvant chemotherapy for breast cancer: T 38.4, HR 106, rigors, neutrophils 0.3. NICE CG151: acute medical emergency, empiric piperacillin-tazobactam immediately.

inputs.hpi: Wide local excision and sentinel node biopsy 3 months ago; now day 9 of cycle 3 of adjuvant docetaxel-cyclophosphamide. Since this morning shivering and feverish, 38.4 at home. Sore mouth. No cough, no urinary symptoms, wound healed. Came to the surgical follow-up appointment rather than calling the oncology hotline.

exam.skin: Healed breast and axillary scars; PICC line site clean.

surgicalHistory: Wide local excision and sentinel lymph node biopsy (3 months ago)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Neutropenic sepsis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Febrile neutropenia (neutrophils 0.3) on chemotherapy - neutropenic sepsis: empiric piperacillin-tazobactam now, oncology informed.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Acute Cholecystitis | 2. Acute Cholangitis | 3. Acute Appendicitis; also in web.symptomInference#1, web.passive#1. PANE has no sepsis or febrile-neutropenia node.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: lib/pane-engine: add sepsis (source-agnostic) as a must-not-miss node driven by physiology, or show a sepsis banner above the PANE list when NEWS2 >=5 with a suspected infection.

guideline.name: NICE CG151 - Neutropenic sepsis: prevention and management in people with cancer
guideline.section: 1.3: treat suspected neutropenic sepsis as an acute medical emergency and offer empiric antibiotic therapy immediately; piperacillin with tazobactam monotherapy as initial empiric therapy
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. CG151. London: NICE; 2012.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021
guideline.section: Screening: recommend against qSOFA alone compared with SIRS, NEWS or MEWS; antimicrobials within 1 h for possible septic shock or high likelihood of sepsis; blood cultures before antimicrobials; lactate measurement; 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid within 3 h for sepsis-induced hypoperfusion or septic shock; noradrenaline first-line vasopressor, MAP target 65 mmHg
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063-e1143.

rationale: Immunosuppressed permutation: febrile neutropenia is an emergency regardless of how well the patient looks; the surgical follow-up setting is where it can be treated as "a bit of a temperature".
